scenes.title: LAG()
scenes.narration: LAG lets a row look backward to read the value of a preceding row within its partition, the classic tool for computing deltas.

scenes.title: How LAG() Works
bullets: Returns a value from a row that comes before the current one
Offset defaults to 1 — the immediately preceding row
Default value is returned when no prior row exists
scenes.narration: LAG returns a value from a row that appears before the current row in the ordered partition. Like LEAD, it takes the column, an optional offset, and an optional default. The offset defaults to one, meaning the immediately preceding row. At the start of a partition there is no prior row, so LAG returns your supplied default or null.

scenes.title: Comparing to the Previous Month
scenes.code:
SELECT
  month,
  revenue,
  LAG(revenue, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_revenue,
  revenue - LAG(revenue, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS mom_change
FROM monthly_revenue;
scenes.narration: This query orders monthly revenue and uses LAG to fetch the previous month's revenue onto each row. Here we pass a default of zero, so the very first month treats its prior value as zero instead of null. Subtracting the previous revenue from the current revenue yields the month-over-month change directly. This pattern is the standard way to compute period-over-period deltas.

scenes.title: Detecting Value Changes
scenes.code:
SELECT
  sensor_id,
  reading_time,
  status,
  LAG(status) OVER (
    PARTITION BY sensor_id
    ORDER BY reading_time
  ) AS prev_status
FROM sensor_log;
scenes.narration: Here we partition sensor readings by sensor and order them by time. LAG of status brings each sensor's previous status onto the current row. By comparing status to prev_status you can flag exactly when a sensor changed state. Because we partition by sensor, one sensor's readings never leak into another's, and each sensor's earliest reading has a null previous status.

scenes.title: Computing a Delta With LAG()
steps: Partition and order the rows by time
LAG pulls the prior row's value onto the current row
Subtract prior from current to get the change
Handle the first row with a default value
scenes.narration: To compute a delta you first partition and order the rows by time. LAG then pulls the prior value onto the current row so both live together. Subtracting the prior value from the current one gives the change. Finally, supply a default so the first row of each partition produces a sensible result rather than null.

scenes.text: LAG() is your go-to for previous-period comparisons and running deltas — pair it with a default value and always define ORDER BY so 'previous' is well defined.
scenes.narration: Use LAG for previous-period comparisons and running deltas, always defining ORDER BY so that previous has a clear meaning.
